entries.text: Concrete work was recorded today, but the available evidence was not clear enough to publish a more specific summary.

Shipped a batch of visit-tracking improvements on the personal site — browser fingerprint diagnostics, an IP lookup link, paged history tables, and a backfill of pre-tracking views from server logs. Also built an isolated demo phone line for Boréal's missed-call-text-back offer with Twilio signature checks and a French demo script, and landed a local company-factory experiment MVP on Genesis.

Added visitor tracking to the personal site, including a password-protected dev dashboard with a geographic view of where visits come from. Kept building out Commander's demo workspace for Boréal's offer too — fixed a mobile layout bug, hardened how demo progress gets saved, and wrote down clearer rules for how it gets deployed.

Built more of Boréal Numérique’s outreach and warm-up system: CRM tracking, demo verification cleanup, and a fuller collateral registry for email-to-call workflows. Also tightened the operating layer around portfolio reports, live asks, and project decision flow so the dashboard work can surface the right work without exposing private client context.

Built more of the shared builder control layer: project status, weekly capacity, and active work threads are now easier to see from one place. Also hardened the bridge that lets the local project system read operational context without giving it write access, and set up a private Slack workflow so project updates can move through a clearer channel instead of staying scattered.

Built a Boréal Insights area in the command dashboard and tightened the registry behind it so malformed notes do not break the view. The work also cleaned up the research notes so unverified CRM observations are labeled as hypotheses instead of facts, and separated outreach constraints from delivery limits.

Shipped the DickFit app into the personal site and tightened its positioning around program outcomes instead of measurement. Also added a bounded jailbreak evaluation console and improved Boréal outreach collateral so drafts stay honest, evidence-based, and do not go out with unfinished placeholders.

Worked on Commander and Boréal outreach tooling: added a clearer follow-up outcome for leads who were sent information, surfaced call options directly in the lead widget, and tightened how call notes survive live refreshes. Also built more flexible outreach email formats and cleaned up collateral so the next step feels simpler and less like a hard sell.

Updated the personal site with a more honest archive of projects and money experiments. Tightened the Commander money-flow research workflow so it focuses less on big abstract markets and more on concrete anomalies, capture paths, and validation gaps. Also scoped Muse as a possible narrow worker for creative and review tasks, rather than as a core operating system.

Built and hardened several parts of Commander, including a local-first PGP workbench, clearer decrypt flow, tighter trust boundaries, and more resilient worker handling. Also refined the Learning workflow so capability gaps and operational failures are treated separately, and tightened Money Flows cleanup and reconciliation behavior. On the personal site, the music page was temporarily disabled and then restored.

Built out a more governed market-probe system for testing small service ideas before committing deeper work. Also tightened Genesis call workflows with safer triggers, scheduled nudges, and guided outreach support, while improving Boréal delivery flows for service selection, contracts, and payment setup.

Worked on Boréal’s client delivery flow: signed-agreement onboarding, live-payment scaffolding, owner notifications, follow-up reminders, and weekly digest pieces moved into place. Separate Signaler work updated the content-sourcing path after an upstream API change and added a small trend-seed pilot. Also tightened a Genesis voice workflow so spoken messages can surface as local desktop notifications.

Shipped a profile view on the Boréal leads workbench, adding a quick-access hook and detail panel to the list/detail interface, plus a fix for a UI bug where the dashboard would blank out briefly during live refreshes. Also brought a new content-agent project, Signaler, under version control alongside the rest of the workspace.

Unified the scattered per-lead views in Boréal's operations dashboard into a single profile: one record and one panel that pulls together everything known about a lead instead of three inconsistent widgets doing the same job differently. Also sketched a renewal proposal for one of the ongoing trading research threads. Small step, but it removes a chunk of friction from the daily workflow of following up with leads.

Shipped a read-only client-portal dashboard for Boréal that fails closed when data snapshots go stale, added test coverage for the multi-turn reply pipeline, and fixed a couple of close-agent edge cases — a dangling opt-out phrase and a price-objection response that wasn't actually grounded in the generated text. Also spent time hardening the Workstreams hub: added an execution/effect ledger and portfolio registry, derived conservative hazard projections from it, and closed a fail-open bug in the resume-status gating logic.

Consolidated the Boréal Numérique operations tooling: retired stale legacy pipeline/stage columns from the CRM, unified several workspace views into one operations dashboard, and hardened its navigation and collateral previews. Also fixed a Nix build habit that was quietly copying ignored files into the store on every change.

Busy build day across several tracks: hardened evidence integrity and shipped a new detection dashboard in Aperture, added a governed workstreams control plane to Commander with a dedicated Boréal section, and stood up a model-matched control plane plus a new behavior-research track in Realm. Also locked in the first research lane for the trading system, narrowing toward a specific on-chain buyer pattern, and made progress on the groundwork for wallet-based copy-trading research.

Spent the day tightening operational plumbing across a couple of projects. On Capital Map, fixed how follow-up reminders are scheduled and reported, and wrote up the launch of a design-partner outreach pipeline. On Boréal, cleaned up overdue callback reminders and put together new client-facing collateral. Also closed out a feasibility check on pulling exchange data for a trading research project — came back negative, so that avenue is shelved for now.

Spent the day hardening the autonomous trading canary system after an audit turned up a real flaw: left unchecked, it would keep repeating the same strategy and burn through its own capital. Added an adaptive capital controller, paused uneconomic research, and locked new strategy runs behind hard cost and expected-edge thresholds. Also shipped a capability control plane and a new research console in Commander to start tracking which tools and skills actually earn their keep.

Spent the day hardening the live capital-canary system for the agent-economy experiment, getting it back to an armed, autonomous, reboot-persistent state. Also worked on the Hyperliquid market-making canary on the onchain terminal project, adding a governed L2 capture job and documenting a source expiry issue after the exchange dropped its long-lived WebSocket connections mid-window.

Closed out a monthly SPY volatility-management strategy after it failed its statistical bar — the returns looked directionally right but the confidence interval didn't clear zero, so it got formally rejected and the reasoning was written up rather than quietly dropped. Alongside that, spent time researching how other people structure and visualize trading algorithms, and recovered an automated paper-trading research loop after a computer crash, making sure it picked back up from its last checkpoint instead of redoing finished work.

Built out the onchain terminal's watchlist and layout system — wallets and cohorts can now be saved, versioned, and reloaded, and position history is reconstructed cleanly from raw exchange fills. On the trading research side, a monthly volatility-managed exposure strategy went through the full preregistered evaluation pipeline and was rejected on statistical grounds, a clean scientific close rather than a bug. Also kicked off a new experiment repo meant to run more of these evaluations in parallel going forward.

Fixed a dashboard loading bug on the trading terminal and shipped richer event filtering — cohort-level accumulation/distribution/flip signals, plus filters by direction, size, leverage, confidence, and time window. Also funded and armed a small paper-to-live canary wallet to start testing autonomous trade execution end-to-end, and wrote up research findings on factor models and borrow-rate depth for the next research lane.

Built a funding and analytics screen in Commander for an experimental autonomous trading agent — a deposit view with wallet status and trackers for how money will move once funded. The agent itself stays deliberately blocked from live trading until manually funded, so for now it just runs its research loop on a timer. Also spent some time fact-checking a viral post claiming an autonomous trading bot turned a small stake into a big overnight win — the underlying article didn't hold up once actually read.

Shipped versioned cohort exposure aggregates and continued building out the Hyperliquid onchain intelligence terminal, adding a strict versioned schema for comparative smart-money cohort definitions with locked-down fields and match rules. Also pushed forward the paper-trading research loop and an operational-intelligence review pass looking for evidence-backed leverage on the current bottleneck.

Added an evidence-backed system model for Realm and wired it into Aperture's workflow atlas, giving a clearer picture of how the pieces connect. Also validated a context-economy optimization for a low-compute agent loop — a paired-trial test showed a sizable cut in token usage and inference cost with no loss in reliability. Rounded out the day with research scaffolding for an equity data pipeline and some inspiration-gathering for trading tools.

Kept pushing SignalToMind's YouTube pipeline forward, getting a private canary video through the full upload-and-thumbnail flow and starting work on persisted state for the account-creation screen. Also drafted a preregistered hypothesis for a new strategy in the trading research pipeline.

Also closed out the first version of a personal trading algorithm — ended the run, reviewed the results, and built infrastructure to test multiple algorithm versions side by side. Separately, tightened remote access security on a personal server, narrowing which devices can reach it.

Archived the brain-monitor dashboard, a self-evolving TUI with an embedded agent, after capturing its design in documentation. Ran a Syntra ops-watch pass to keep the intelligence layer current without touching the active pipeline.

Set up GitNexus across the active codebases and started scoping a native graph visualization island for the Aperture dashboard. On the SYNTRA side, made a task launchable from the panel and added a relaunch path for failed jobs.

On the side, reorganized a local music library by sorting tracks into per-album folders named by release year. A few task specs were drafted and live state was reviewed.

On the automation side, added launch gates and a required-inputs form for SYNTRA, and sketched a small architect agent that reviews each completed executor task and reports back over Telegram.

Consolidated the Boréal codebase into a single monorepo and wired up a missed-call text-back — any inbound call now triggers an automatic SMS reply. Set up hourly database backups and tracked the supporting infrastructure as durable, named services. Also refreshed the personal site with updated project and employer pages, linked public repositories, and cleaned up the taskboard so cancelled and split work no longer clutters the active list.

Spent the day hardening Aperture, the task-execution layer that runs agent work. The recurring problem was jobs failing silently and finished tasks still showing as ready, so the work went into honest status reporting — capturing when an executor is actually blocked, recording real completion, and deriving each job's writable scope from its brief instead of guessing. Also added a live next-actions feed so the current state of the queue is visible at a glance.

Resumed Boréal after a full ecosystem audit and restored its inbound lead pipeline end to end, including fixing two operations-control bugs that had made recovery impossible. A deeper audit then exposed conflicting CRM state, misclassified leads, overlapping follow-up systems, and no single outbound send gate, so automated sending stayed off while the remediation work was scoped. Also verified SYNTRA's path-based product routes live in production and cleared out obsolete project infrastructure.

Most of the day went into Aperture, the task orchestration board: it moved to React, got live log streaming, dependency gates between tasks, and a proper failure badge when a job exits badly. The personal site also picked up a batch of fixes around the writing feed and music pages. On the SYNTRA side, a few delegated implementation tasks landed, including path-based routing with pre-rendering.

Aperture's taskboard gained full brief previews, persistent controls, smoother polling, and live Codex launch and monitoring. SYNTRA moved to path-based routing with static pre-rendering and closed its remaining phase-one blockers. The personal site restored its complete X post history, streamed seeded posts into the writing feed, and improved music navigation.

Reworked the personal site's reading page into collapsible learning paths, expanded the curriculum from the local ebook library, and organized it into a four-tier progression. Also added a Goodreads profile link and improved how expanded paths stay in view.

The personal site got a meaningful round of updates: a social feed with threaded replies, timestamps, and pagination was wired in, and the writing feed and daily log now update automatically. A taskboard interface (Aperture) was deployed as a live ops tool. Genesis — an autonomous agent infrastructure layer — was initialized with a daemon and identity stack. Work also began on SYNTRA, a new project, including a database migration and a business model pivot toward running a full storefront rather than a redirect-based affiliate setup.

Spent the last couple days building out the personal site's /log feature — a daily, auto-generated public record of what I'm actually working on, gathered, summarized, and sanitized before it ever hits the page. Also rebuilt the writing tab to pull in my own posts and music listening, which meant wrestling with unreliable third-party feeds: settled on caching every fetched post into a small database so the page survives when the upstream sources go down. Fixed a keyboard-nav bug that was swallowing browser shortcuts along the way.
Genesis given persistent memory across sessions and its own terminal goals. Ongoing.
Boréal Numérique paused — outreach ran its course, one discovery call booked. Case-study gap still open.
